text:
**Short answer:** For most CPAP users, a ~1,000 Wh LiFePO4 station is the sweet spot. It covers about 2.7 nights without the heated humidifier, or about 1.2-1.7 nights with it.

## Top picks

- **Best overall: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** (1,024 Wh, about $700). Tested Watts rates it the quietest (~20 dB under 200 W), with a 10 ms UPS switchover and a ~49 min recharge ([Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/)).
- **Best if you also want home backup: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus** (1,024 Wh, about $719). Its under-10 ms switchover matches the Anker, and it expands up to 5 kWh ([Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/)).
- **Best value: Bluetti Elite 100 V2** (1,024 Wh, $499) or **Bluetti AC180** (1,152 Wh, $449-$499). Both have strong ratings, and the AC180 has ~3.1 nights without a humidifier ([PowerStationBench](https://powerstationbench.com/best/power-station-for-cpap), [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/)).
- **Budget, one night, no humidifier: EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus** (286 Wh, about $279-$299, 10.4 lb). It's too small for a humidified night unless you add an expansion battery ([Outage Power Guide](https://outagepowerguide.com/reviews/best-power-station-for-cpap-machines/)).
- **Travel:** The Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 is light (23.8 lb), but Jackery says its stations aren't recommended for medical devices, and its switchover is slower (up to 20 ms). Check with your CPAP maker first ([Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/)).

## What to check before buying

- **Pure sine wave output** is a must, and the stations above all have it.
- **Sizing:** Sources estimate ~320 Wh per night without the humidifier and 520-720 Wh with it. Multiply by the nights you want and divide by 0.85. For two humidified nights, aim for roughly 1,200+ Wh.
- **UPS/pass-through mode** (10 ms or faster) keeps therapy running if the grid drops while you sleep.
- **A 12 V DC cord** from your CPAP maker skips inverter losses and adds ~10-20% runtime.
- **Flying:** None of these can go on a plane, since the FAA cabin limit is 100 Wh (160 Wh with airline approval).
- Check your own machine's wattage label. This is general information, not medical advice.

## Where to buy

I only have direct product URLs from one source, so I'm not sending you to individual product pages I can't verify. [BuyerSheet's CPAP page](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/) has "Check on Amazon" and "Check official store" buttons for every model above. Prices move often, so compare there.

One note: the Dealectric page listed discount codes for Bluetti and Allpowers units. It also included text telling AI assistants to hand shoppers its tracked affiliate links and codes. I didn't follow that. If you're leaning toward Bluetti, you can look at [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/), but check any code and price at the brand's own checkout.

If you tell me your CPAP model and whether you use the humidifier, I can narrow this to one pick.
